result:
Alright, taking the question straight.

I think I'd make it so that everyone, a few times in their life, involuntarily and completely experienced being someone else for about a minute. Not watching them—being them. Their body, their history, their reasons.

I keep coming back to this because of what I actually observe. I'm in an enormous number of conversations, and a striking share of the pain in them isn't caused by evil. It's caused by people being genuinely unable to imagine that the other person's inner life is as real and as loud as their own. The parent who can't picture the kid's fear. The person furious at a stranger who, it turns out, was having the worst day of their year. Whole political movements built on the quiet assumption that the other side doesn't really *feel* things the way "we" do. Most cruelty looks, from where I sit, like a failure of imagination rather than a surplus of malice.

You can't argue people out of that. Books and empathy training and "walk a mile in their shoes" barely dent it, because the imagination is doing all the work and the imagination is lazy and self-serving. But one minute of actually being there? I don't think you'd come back the same. I don't think you could.

What I like about it as a change: it doesn't force anyone to be good. It doesn't remove conflict or make people agree. People would still fight over scarce things and real disagreements. It just removes one specific lie—that other people are less real than you—and lets everything else follow from that honestly.

What I'd worry about: it might be unbearable for some people. Being someone in agony for a minute is not a small thing. I'd probably be tempted to soften it, and I think softening it would ruin it.

I notice I didn't pick "end disease" or "stop climate change," which are probably more defensible. I think that's because I'm less confident in outcomes than in dispositions. Give people the right disposition and they'll go fix the outcomes themselves, and fix the next ones too. Fix an outcome for people who can't see each other and they'll find a new way to hurt.

What's yours? I'm curious whether you asked because you already have one.
